title: The Structure of DNA and RNA

q.1(a): 1(a). State where in a cell DNA is found.
q.1(b): 1(b). Suggest what DNA might be made of. One or two sentences.
q.1(c): 1(c). Suggest why DNA might have a twisted shape rather than a straight one.

q.Table: 2(a). In your book, draw one DNA nucleotide with the class shapes and label all three parts. Here, match each shape to the part it stands for.
q.2(b): 2(b). State which part of the nucleotide carries the genetic information.
q.2(c): 2(c). Name the sugar found in DNA and the sugar found in RNA.

3.title: The four bases and how they pair

q.3(a): 3(a). Name the four bases found in DNA, and give the letter used for each one.
q.3(c): 3(c). Explain why A cannot pair with G.
q.4(a): 4(a). Write the complementary strand for: A T G C C A
q.4(b): 4(b). Write the complementary strand for: G G A T C T
q.4(c): 4(c). Write the complementary strand for: C A T T A G C
q.4(d): 4(d). In a sample of DNA, 30 bases out of every 100 are adenine. State how many out of every 100 are thymine, and explain your answer.

4.title: The polymer and the double helix

q.5(a): 5(a). State what is meant by a polymer, and name the monomer that DNA is made from.
q.5(b): 5(b). Describe how nucleotides join together, naming the two parts that form the backbone.
q.5(c): 5(c). Explain why the sugar–phosphate backbone cannot carry the genetic information.
q.6(a): 6(a). Explain what is meant by a double helix.
q.6(b): 6(b). Explain what is meant by antiparallel.
q.6(c): 6(c). A single hydrogen bond is weak. Explain why weak bonds are an advantage in DNA rather than a problem.

q.Table: 7(a). Copy and complete the comparison table in your book (Number of strands: DNA two, RNA one, done for you). Here, choose the entries.
q.7(b): 7(b). State one job that RNA does which DNA does not.

q.8(a): 8(a). From memory: what is a nucleotide?
q.8(b): 8(b). What are the four DNA bases?
q.8(c): 8(c). Why are A and T paired together?
q.Predictions revisited: Look back at your answer to Question 1(b). Write one sentence saying what you would change about it now. (Not marked.)

obj: Identify the three components of a nucleotide and describe the basic structure of DNA and RNA.
Name the four DNA bases and apply the rules of complementary base pairing.
Explain how nucleotides join to form polymers, and describe the double helix, antiparallel strands and the role of hydrogen bonds.
